$meta.procedure: Figma variables -> this file is synced by Claude via Figma MCP (see CLAUDE.md / ADR-0010). Then run `pnpm sync:tokens` to regenerate app/theme.css. Never edit app/theme.css by hand.

semantic.$comment: A plain string ref is a light-only token (no dark variant yet). An object { light, dark } carries a dark-mode override. `pnpm sync:tokens` emits the dark refs into a `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }` block in app/theme.css — that attribute is what Ladle's Light/Dark toggle sets on <html> (see @ladle/react's init-side-effects.ts); it's also the hook the real app would use once it grows its own theme switch (not built yet, out of scope for #42). Dark values below are this round's addition (2026-07-20, ticket #42), scoped to the primitives Atom/Button actually uses — no Figma dark-mode frames exist to fetch, so these are derived by staying inside Tailwind's stock stone/red scale rather than inventing one-off hex. Not every token has a dark counterpart yet; that's a flagged gap for a future token-sync pass, not an oversight. TICKET #56 (2026-07-20, supersedes #52's state tier): Figma added a FOURTH state to Button/Default and redistributed the values. What #52 recorded as Hover is now Active (pressed); Hover took a milder new value; Selected no longer changes the background at all — it only darkens the text to `text`. The scale is therefore `role` / `role-hover` / `role-active`, and the `*-selected` colour tokens #52 added (surface-selected, surface-raised-selected, border-selected, priority-urgent-bg-selected) were REMOVED rather than left as dead names — Selected needs no background token. `surface-hover` changed from stone-300 (which had no consumer) to stone-50 and now backs Button/White's Hover; `surface-active` (stone-100) shares its primitive with `surface-muted` but is kept as a separate name because it is a distinct role — a state colour, not a static surface. TICKET #58 (2026-07-20): re-fetched Atom/Input-field (node 3705:4402) expecting it to have been re-bound onto Button's shared border/border-hover/border-active scale now that Figma redistributed a fourth state (Selected) onto it. It has NOT: Default matches Button's Default (stone-300, so it keeps reading the shared `border` token, no component-scoped token needed there), but Hover (stone-500) and the new Active (a value with no prior primitive, added this ticket as `stone-600`) are genuinely different pixels from Button/Outline's Hover (stone-400) and Active (stone-700) — confirmed by fetching both nodes side by side, not assumed. The good news: the #56-era bug (Hover darker than Active, backwards from Button) is gone — Hover (stone-500) is now correctly lighter than Active (stone-600), same direction as Button. So this is no longer a stale/unbound node; it is a deliberately distinct border ramp, kept under its own tokens rather than forced onto Button's. `border-input-focus` is renamed `border-input-active` (it reads Figma's actual `Active` state; the old name described this atom's `:focus-within` *interpretation* of that state, which still holds — see design/figma-map.json). `border-input-hover` keeps its stone-500 value unchanged. Now that this node carries the SAME four state names as Atom/Button, its CSS hooks follow the same semantics Button established in #56, so all four states are modelled: Hover -> `hover:`, Active -> `active:` (Figma's Active means 'being pressed', which is what CSS :active means), Selected -> `:focus-within`. Selected is the state whose sample shows a typed value (text stone-950) rather than the placeholder, i.e. the field has been engaged - which is exactly what :focus-within expresses, and it is a better fit than the pre-#58 reading that put :focus-within on Active. That mapping is still this atom's interpretation (Figma labels states, not CSS hooks) and stays flagged in design/figma-map.json for confirmation. `border-input-selected` (stone-400) backs it. Dark values remain this codebase's own pick (no Figma dark frames exist); the destructive hover/active pair still both resolve to red-950 in dark mode, i.e. those states are invisible there — a known, flagged gap, not an oversight. Figma MCP still returns resolved hex only, never variable names, so every semantic name here is derived from values, not read from Figma.

typography.$comment: Figma text styles are Tailwind-native; no CSS generation needed. This is the authoritative mapping for agents (font: Inter).
